introduction: On this sixth Sunday of Easter, Jesus calls his disciples his friends and gives them his commandment: love one another as I have loved you. John tells us simply that God is love. In the first reading, the Holy Spirit falls on Cornelius and his household, and Peter sees that God shows no partiality. Let us remain in Christ's love and let it reach everyone we meet.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God is love, and he loved us first. Let us bring our prayers to him.
intentions: For the Church: that she may welcome people of every nation and background, knowing that God shows no partiality. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who give their lives for others, at home, at work or in danger: that God may reward their love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel unloved, lonely or rejected: that they may experience the love of God through the friendship of Christians. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peace between peoples and an end to prejudice: that we may see every person as someone God loves. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may love one another as Jesus has loved us, and that our joy may be full. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of love, you sent your Son so that we might live through him. Keep us in his love, and make us faithful friends of Jesus and of one another. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: I have called you friends
reflection.body:
The Gospel today is from the Last Supper, the night before Jesus died. He speaks to his disciples about love, and the words are full of tenderness. "Even as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you. Remain in my love."

He gives them a commandment, but it is a strange one, because love cannot be forced: "This is my commandment, that you love one another, even as I have loved you." The measure is his own love, and he tells them what that means: "Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends." The next day he did exactly that.

Then he changes the way he speaks about them: "No longer do I call you servants... But I have called you friends." And he reminds them who took the first step: "You didn't choose me, but I chose you."

John's letter puts it in three words: "God is love." And he makes sure we do not get it backwards: "In this is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us." Our love is always an answer.

The first reading shows how far that love reaches. Peter enters the house of Cornelius, a Roman centurion, something a devout Jew would normally avoid. While he is still speaking, the Holy Spirit falls on everyone listening. Peter had already understood: "Truly I perceive that God doesn't show favoritism." He baptizes them all.

Jesus says he tells us these things "that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be made full." Love is the way to joy. This week, think of one person you find hard to love, and do one concrete thing for their good. And thank Jesus for choosing you as his friend.
